mainTopic: מעשר בהמה: mistakes in counting, and two animals that leave the pen together
overview: The גמרא discusses מעשר בהמה when the owner counts wrong. A ברייתא learns from the פסוק that an animal mistakenly called 'tenth' becomes holy, but only if it is right next to the real tenth (the ninth or the eleventh). Another ברייתא says only one mistaken animal can become holy. The גמרא explains that this follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who treats a mistake like a תמורה and holds that a second תמורה does not work. רבא then rules on two animals leaving the pen together: depending on what the owner calls them, a holy animal ends up mixed with another animal. רב כהנא and רב אשי debate whether animals that leave at the same time both become holy, even though the name 'tenth' was never taken away. They test this against the משנה's 'זה הכלל' and a ברייתא, and the discussion leads to רבי's view that calling the tenth 'eleventh' does not remove its name when the owner has many animals. Finally, three ברייתות give different rulings for two mixed animals: graze, be sacrificed, or die. The 'graze' ruling is assigned to the רבנן, and the other two are explained on the next amud.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the mixed-up count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of an owner who calls the ninth 'tenth', the tenth 'ninth', and the eleventh 'tenth'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he called the ninth animal 'tenth', the tenth 'ninth', and the eleventh 'tenth'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the משנה so it can start discussing it. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מעשר בהמה the animals pass under a rod one at a time, and the tenth becomes holy. Here the owner counted wrong. The משנה rules that all three animals become holy: the ninth is eaten once it gets a blemish, the tenth is מעשר, and the eleventh is brought as a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The animal tithe: every tenth animal of the flock or herd is holy
Ninth
Tenth
Eleventh

phrases.english: If he called the ninth 'tenth',
and the tenth 'ninth',
and the eleventh 'tenth'.
phrases.notes: In the משנה the ruling continues: all three are holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of this line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the count is mixed up this way, the ninth, tenth, and eleventh are all holy.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks for the source
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks where we learn that all three animals become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: From where do we know that if he called the ninth 'tenth', the tenth 'ninth', and the eleventh 'tenth', all three are holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that asks for the source in the תורה for the משנה's ruling. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally only the real tenth animal is holy. So it is surprising that an animal which is not really tenth becomes holy just because it was called 'tenth' by mistake. That is why a פסוק is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know? (asks for a source)
Are holy

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: From where do we know
that if he called the ninth 'tenth',
and the tenth 'ninth',
and the eleventh 'tenth',
that all three of them are holy?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for the source behind the ruling of the משנה quoted in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה that the mistakenly named animals also become holy.

steps.title: The verse is the source
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא quotes the פסוק about מעשר בהמה as the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And all the tithe of the herd or the flock, whatever passes under the rod, the tenth shall be holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a פסוק from ויקרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'the tenth shall be holy' is read broadly. It covers the real tenth animal, and also an animal that the owner named 'tenth'. That is how the mistaken animals become holy too.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces the proof-text)
The rod the animals pass under while they are counted
Shall be holy

phrases.english: The verse states:
'And all the tithe of the herd or the flock,
whatever passes under the rod,
the tenth shall be holy'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'the tenth shall be holy' includes an animal that was called tenth, even by mistake.

steps.title: Maybe even the eighth and twelfth are included?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a possibility: maybe the פסוק also includes the eighth or the twelfth if they were called 'tenth'.
steps.simpleTranslation: I might have thought that I include even the eighth and the twelfth?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא suggests that the rule might stretch too far. It is setting up a limit that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If calling an animal 'tenth' is what makes it holy, then any animal called 'tenth' might become holy, even one far from the real tenth. The ברייתא raises this idea in order to reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: I might have thought (introduces a possibility that will be rejected)
Include
Eighth

phrases.english: One might think that I include
even the eighth and the twelfth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the inclusion from step 3 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the broad reading of the פסוק also covers animals further from the tenth.

steps.title: Only animals right next to the tenth
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא limits the rule: the mistaken animal must be right next to the tenth, so only the ninth or the eleventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said: since the tenth is holy and its mistake also becomes holy, then just as the tenth itself becomes holy only when it is 'close' (it really is the tenth), so too its mistake becomes holy only when it is close to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the possibility from step 4 and says no. Only the animals next to the tenth can become holy by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mistake is compared to the real tenth. The real tenth becomes holy only because it is exactly at the number ten. So the mistaken animal must also be close to ten, meaning the ninth or the eleventh, and not the eighth or the twelfth.

keyTerms.meaning: Since
Its mistake: the animal wrongly called 'tenth'
Close by, right next to it

steps.whatToRemember: An animal called 'tenth' by mistake becomes holy only if it is the ninth or the eleventh, right next to the real tenth.

phrases.english: You said: since it (the tenth) is holy,
and its mistake also becomes holy,

phrases.aramaic: מָה הוּא אֵינוֹ מְקוּדָּשׁ אֶלָּא בְּסָמוּךְ,
phrases.english: just as it is holy only when close,

phrases.aramaic: אַף טָעוּתוֹ אֵינָהּ מִתְקַדֶּשֶׁת אֶלָּא בְּסָמוּךְ.
phrases.english: so too its mistake becomes holy only when close.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possibility raised in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mistake is compared to the real tenth, so only the animals next to it (the ninth and the eleventh) are included.

steps.title: A ברייתא says only one mistaken animal becomes holy
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא that says the mistake is 'unique', just like the tenth. That suggests only one extra animal can become holy, not both the ninth and the eleventh.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught: just as it (the tenth) is unique, so too its mistake is unique!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a challenge. Another ברייתא seems to say that only one mistaken animal can become holy, which clashes with the משנה where both the ninth and the eleventh become holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is only one real tenth animal. If the mistake is compared to it, there should also be only one mistaken animal. But our משנה makes both the ninth and the eleventh holy, so the two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Unique, only one

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two comparisons. Step 5 compared the mistake to the tenth in 'closeness' (it must be next to the tenth). This ברייתא compares them in 'uniqueness' (only one). The first limits which animals can count. The second limits how many.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
just as it is unique (only one),
so too its mistake is unique!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's ruling (step 1) that both the ninth and the eleventh become holy.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the ninth and the eleventh can both become holy by mistake.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא compares the mistake to the tenth in being 'unique'. Since there is only one tenth, only one mistaken animal should become holy.

steps.title: The 'unique' ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recited before רבי יוחנן that the ברייתא limiting the mistake to one animal follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. He holds that the eleventh becomes holy only if the owner was silent at the ninth.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רבי יוחנן: Whose view is this ברייתא? It is רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: the eleventh never becomes holy unless the owner stayed silent at the ninth, then called the tenth 'ninth' and the eleventh 'tenth.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 6. The ברייתא that allows only one mistaken animal belongs to one particular תנא, רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון. It is not the view of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says both the ninth and the eleventh can become holy. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees: the eleventh can become holy only if no mistake was made at the ninth. So if he already wrongly called the ninth 'tenth,' the eleventh cannot become holy as well. That is why the mistake is 'unique.'

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? (a question asking which תנא the source follows)
It never happens that…
That he stays silent (he did not call the ninth 'tenth')
The eleventh animal

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'silent at the ninth' does not mean he said nothing at all during the count. It means he did not mistakenly call the ninth animal 'tenth.' Only then can the eleventh become holy.

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rabbi Yoḥanan:
phrases.notes: A תנא here is a reciter of ברייתות in the study hall.

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
The eleventh never becomes holy
unless he was silent at the ninth,
phrases.notes: He did not call the ninth 'tenth.'

phrases.english: and he calls the tenth 'ninth,'
and the eleventh 'tenth.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּאנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by assigning the challenging ברייתא to a different תנא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution to a dissenting תנא (the source follows a different opinion than our משנה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'unique' ברייתא seemed to contradict our משנה, which lets both the ninth and the eleventh become holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, who allows only one mistaken animal. Our משנה follows a different view, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Why only one mistaken animal: a mistake works like substitution
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds like רבי יהודה, that a counting mistake in מעשר works like a תמורה. He also holds like his father רבי שמעון, that one cannot make a second תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי יהודה, who says a mistake in מעשר is a תמורה. And he holds like his father, who says: one cannot substitute and then substitute again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view from the last step. He combines two earlier opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step one: according to רבי יהודה, wrongly calling an animal 'tenth' makes it holy the way a תמורה does. Step two: according to רבי שמעון, after one substitution, a second substitution does not work. So once the ninth became holy through the mistake, calling the eleventh 'tenth' has no effect.

keyTerms.meaning: A mistake in counting the tithe animal
Substitution: an animal that becomes holy because someone tried to swap it for a holy animal
Like his father (רבי שמעון)
One cannot substitute and then substitute again

steps.whatToRemember: Only one mistaken animal can become holy according to רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון because of two ideas together: a mistake = תמורה (רבי יהודה), and no second תמורה (רבי שמעון).
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the root of the disagreement. Our משנה does not treat the mistake as a limited one-time תמורה, so both the ninth and the eleventh can become holy.

phrases.english: He holds like Rabbi Yehuda, who says:
a mistake in the tithe is a substitution,
and he holds like his father, who says:
one cannot substitute and then substitute again.
phrases.notes: A second substitution for the same holy animal does not take effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר: טָעוּת מַעֲשֵׂר תְּמוּרָה הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the opinion named in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the logic of the opinion behind the answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was unclear why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון would block the eleventh after a mistake at the ninth.
steps.terutzMaskana: A mistake works like a תמורה, and a second תמורה does not work. So only the first mistaken animal becomes holy.

steps.title: Two animals come out as the ninth and both are called 'ninth'
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if two animals leave the pen together as the ninth and he calls both 'ninth,' the holy tenth is mixed with a regular animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If two animals came out together as the ninth and he called them both 'ninth,' then the tenth and a regular animal are mixed together. The tenth is holy on its own. The ninth he called 'ninth,' so it stays regular.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ruling from רבא about two animals leaving the pen at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two animals come out together at the ninth spot, one counts as the ninth and the other as the tenth. The real tenth is holy automatically, even though he called it 'ninth.' The ninth is regular because he correctly called it 'ninth.' Since nobody knows which animal is which, the holy one and the regular one are mixed.

keyTerms.meaning: Two animals came out (of the pen) together
Regular, non-holy animals
Mixed up with each other; we cannot tell which is which
Holy on its own, even without being named correctly

steps.confusionAlert: Calling the real tenth 'ninth' does not cancel its holiness. The tenth animal becomes holy just by being tenth, whatever name the owner says.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If two came out as the ninth,
and he called them 'ninth' —
the tenth and a non-holy animal are mixed with each other,
since the tenth is holy on its own,
and the ninth, he called it 'ninth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case after the previous discussion was resolved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If two animals come out as the ninth and both are called 'ninth,' the holy tenth and a regular animal are mixed.

steps.title: Two animals come out as the ninth and both are called 'tenth'
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: if he calls both animals 'tenth,' the real tenth and the ninth are mixed, because he called both of them 'tenth.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he called them both 'tenth,' then the tenth and the ninth are mixed together. What is the reason? He called both of them 'tenth.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the second half of his ruling: the same case, but this time the owner calls both animals 'tenth.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real tenth is holy as מעשר. The ninth also gets holiness because he wrongly called it 'tenth,' like the mistake case in our משנה. So both animals are holy, but in different ways. Since we cannot tell which is which, neither can be brought as an offering. Both are left to graze until they get a מום.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Both of them

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule: calling both 'ninth' mixes the holy tenth with a regular animal. Calling both 'tenth' mixes the tenth with the ninth, which became holy through the mistake. Either way, we cannot tell them apart.

phrases.english: If he called them 'tenth,'
the tenth and the ninth are mixed with each other.
What is the reason?
He called both of them 'tenth.'
phrases.notes: The ninth gets holiness from the mistaken name.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְרָאָן ״עֲשִׂירִי״, עֲשִׂירִי וּתְשִׁיעִי מְעוֹרָבִין זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of רבא's ruling, contrasting with step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If two animals come out as the ninth and both are called 'tenth,' the tenth and the ninth (holy through the mistake) are mixed.

steps.title: Two animals leave together as the tenth
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues. If two animals leave together at the tenth spot and he calls both 'tenth,' the tenth and the eleventh are mixed together. If he calls both 'eleventh,' the tenth and a regular animal are mixed together.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two animals came out together as the tenth and he called them both 'tenth,' the tenth and the eleventh are mixed with each other. If he called them both 'eleventh,' the tenth and a regular animal are mixed with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his third case. This time the two animals leave together at the tenth spot instead of the ninth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One of the two animals is the real tenth. The other is really the eleventh. If he calls both 'tenth,' the real tenth is מעשר, and the eleventh that was called 'tenth' also becomes holy, but with a different kind of holiness. We cannot tell which animal is which, so they are mixed. If he calls both 'eleventh,' the real tenth is holy anyway, the other animal stays חולין, and again we cannot tell them apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The tenth animal, which becomes holy as מעשר
The eleventh animal
A regular, non-holy animal
Mixed up with each other, so we cannot tell which is which

phrases.english: Two animals came out together as the tenth
and he called them both 'tenth'
the tenth and the eleventh
are mixed with each other.
If he called them both 'eleventh,'
the tenth and a regular animal
are mixed with each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third case in רבא's series, after his two cases of animals leaving together as the ninth
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two animals leaving together at the tenth spot: called 'tenth' means the tenth and eleventh are mixed; called 'eleventh' means the tenth and a regular animal are mixed.

steps.title: Why do we need this extra case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed this case. It seems to be the same as the earlier case of the ninth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this further case? It is the same as that earlier one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבא said this case at all. It is setting up an answer that will show the case teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, two animals left together and both became holy. The same reasoning seems to work here, so the new case looks unnecessary. The גמרא wants to find what this case adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this extra statement?
This is the same as that one

phrases.english: Why do I need this further case?
It is the same as that one!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא תּוּ לְמָה לִי? הַיְינוּ הָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רבא's tenth-spot case adds beyond his ninth-spot cases
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new law the tenth-spot case teaches

steps.title: Both become holy even though 'tenth' was not removed
steps.stepSummary: The case teaches that whenever two animals leave together, both become holy. This is true even though the name 'tenth' was never taken away from the real tenth.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: whenever they leave at the same time, both become holy, even though the name 'tenth' was not taken away from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The tenth-spot case teaches a new point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has a rule: as long as the name 'tenth' is still on the real tenth, an eleventh called 'tenth' does not become holy. In the ninth-spot case there was no eleventh at all, so that rule never came up. Here the real tenth keeps the name 'tenth,' yet the eleventh called 'tenth' still becomes holy. So when animals leave at the same time, the משנה's rule does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it comes to teach us
At the same time
The name 'tenth' was taken away

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the coming challenge, because it seems to go against the 'זה הכלל' rule in the משנה.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
that whenever they leave at the same time
both of them become holy,
even though it was not taken away,
the name 'tenth,' from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what the extra case adds
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Same-time leaving makes both animals holy even when the name 'tenth' stays on the real tenth

steps.title: רב אשי challenges from the rule in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא taught this law. רב אשי challenged him: the name 'tenth' was never taken away, and the משנה says that in such a case the eleventh does not become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא sat and taught this law. רב אשי said to רב כהנא: But the name 'tenth' was not taken away from it! And we learned in the משנה, 'This is the rule: whenever the name tenth was not taken away from it, the eleventh is not holy.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רבא's law, which רב כהנא was teaching, using the general rule in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule is clear: if the real tenth still has the name 'tenth,' the eleventh does not become holy. In רבא's case the real tenth still has the name 'tenth,' yet רבא says the eleventh is holy. This seems to go directly against the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A taught law or teaching
This is the general rule
Becomes holy

phrases.english: Rav Kahana sat
and taught this law.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:
But it was not taken away,
the name 'tenth,' from it!
And we learned: 'This is the rule:
whenever it was not taken away,
the name 'tenth,' from it,
the eleventh is not holy!'

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא לֹא נֶעֱקַר שֵׁם עֲשִׂירִי הֵימֶנּוּ, וּתְנַן זֶה הַכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the new point just learned in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's law that both animals become holy when they leave at the same time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's general rule says the eleventh is not holy as long as the name 'tenth' stays on the real tenth, which is exactly what happens in רבא's case

steps.title: The rule only applies one after the other
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the משנה's rule applies only when the animals leave one after the other. When they leave at the same time, both become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: That applies only when they leave one after the other. But when they leave at the same time, both of them become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא defends רבא by limiting the משנה's rule to one kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'the name tenth was not taken away' is about animals that leave in order. A same-time case is different: both animals are named at once, so both become holy. This way רבא and the משנה do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: This applies only to...
One after the other

phrases.english: That applies only when they leave one after the other.
But when they leave at the same time,
both of them become holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּזֶה אַחַר זֶה, אֲבָל בְּבַת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the משנה's rule is restricted to animals leaving one after the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's rule covers every case, including animals that leave at the same time
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only animals leaving one after the other; animals leaving at the same time both become holy

steps.title: The one-after-the-other case is already written outright
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks רב כהנא's answer. The משנה already spells out the one-after-the-other case, so the extra words 'זה הכלל' must add something else. That seems to be the same-time case.
steps.simpleTranslation: One after the other? The משנה states that case outright: 'If he called the ninth tenth, and the tenth tenth, and the eleventh tenth, the eleventh is not holy.' So what does 'This is the rule' come to add? Does it not come to add the case of leaving at the same time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא's answer from the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'זה הכלל' usually adds cases that were not already stated. The one-after-the-other case is already written in the משנה. So 'זה הכלל' seems to add the same-time case and to say that there, too, the eleventh is not holy. That goes against רבא.

steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16 the attack said 'זה הכלל' must be adding the same-time case, which would work against רב כהנא. רב כהנא answers that it adds a silent-owner case instead. steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא that two animals leaving together are both holy
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that when two animals leave together and are called 'tenth,' the tenth and eleventh are mixed together and both are holy. This holds even though the name 'tenth' was never taken away. That supports רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you do not say this, what about the ברייתא? It teaches: two animals went out as the tenth, neither one went before the other, and he called them 'tenth.' Then the tenth and the eleventh are mixed up with each other. But the name 'tenth' was never taken away from the real tenth! It must be because we say that whenever they leave at the same time, both become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב כהנא's rule. In it, two animals leave together and both become holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא the owner never called the real tenth by another name, yet the eleventh still becomes holy as שלמים. It is mixed up with the tenth, which is holy as מעשר. The only way to explain this is רב כהנא's rule: leaving at the same time makes both holy.

steps.title: רב אשי reads the ברייתא as a case where the name was taken away

steps.simpleTranslation: If that is the reason, it is no proof. What case are we dealing with here? One of them went first and put its head out, and he called it 'eleventh.' Then it got mixed back in, the two came out together, and he called them 'tenth.' Here the name 'tenth' was taken away from the real tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects the proof from the ברייתא. He explains it with a special case that fits the משנה's rule without needing רב כהנא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי says the eleventh became holy in the ברייתא for a different reason. The real tenth had already been called 'eleventh,' so its name 'tenth' was taken away. Then the משנה's own rule explains why the eleventh becomes holy, and leaving together does not matter.

steps.title: But the ברייתא says neither went first

steps.title: 'Did not go first' means it went back in

steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'neither went first' mean? That it went back and got mixed in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what the words 'לא קדם' really mean, which saves רב אשי's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's words do not deny that one animal poked its head out. They mean it did not end up leaving first, because it went back in and mixed with the others. So רב אשי's reading stands, and the ברייתא is no proof for רב כהנא.

But רבי holds that saying 'eleventh' is not an עקירה, meaning it does not remove the name. So it seems this reading of the ברייתא goes against רבי, and that is a problem.

steps.title: רבי's rule applies only when there are many animals
steps.stepSummary: The reading can fit רבי. His rule that 'eleventh' does not remove the name applies only when the owner has many animals. Here he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי. רבי said his rule only where the owner has many animals, because then we say he meant 'חד עישורא,' one tithe-group. Here he does not have more animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא can still follow רבי. רבי's rule is limited to an owner who has many animals.

So the owner may simply mean 'this finishes one group of ten,' and the name 'tenth' stays. When there are no more animals, there is no second group to talk about. Then 'eleventh' really means eleventh, and even רבי agrees it removes the name 'tenth.'

steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's rule is that the eleventh can become holy only if the real tenth has lost its name 'tenth.' He says the eleventh is not holy here, so he must hold that calling the tenth 'eleventh' did not remove its name. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagrees and makes the eleventh holy.

steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, calling the tenth 'eleventh' would seem to take away its name 'tenth.' רבא says that with many animals, the owner may have meant 'one tithe-group,' so the name 'tenth' stays and the eleventh is not holy. This supports the limit given in step 23.

steps.title: Three different rulings on two animals that came out together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the case of two animals that came out together as the tenth. Three ברייתות give three different rulings: the animals graze, they are sacrificed, or they must die.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two came out as the tenth, one ברייתא teaches: they should graze. Another ברייתא teaches: they should be sacrificed. Another ברייתא teaches: they must die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the earlier case and lists three ברייתות that disagree about what to do with the two animals. This sets up the next steps, where the גמרא will try to explain why they disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two animals are mixed together, and both have some holiness. One ברייתא says they graze until they get a blemish. One says they are brought as offerings. One says they must be left to die. The גמרא now has to explain how three rulings on the same case can all be right.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three versions for two animals that came out together as the tenth: graze, be sacrificed, or die.
steps.kashyaTarget: The three ברייתות about two animals that came out together as the tenth, which seem to contradict one another.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same case receives three incompatible rulings (graze, be sacrificed, die), so the ברייתות cannot all be right as they stand.

steps.title: The 'graze' ruling follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא saying the two animals 'graze' follows the רבנן. They hold that one may not bring קדשים into a situation that makes them more likely to become פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not a problem. The ברייתא that says 'they graze' follows the רבנן, who say: you may not bring holy animals into a situation that leads to disqualification.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the contradiction between the three ברייתות by explaining the first one: 'they graze.' This is the first piece of a longer answer, and the other two rulings will be explained next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know which animal is the real מעשר and which is a שלמים. If both were sacrificed, they would have to be eaten under the stricter rules of both kinds of offering, which makes it easier for the meat to become פסול. The רבנן forbid creating that risk, so neither animal is sacrificed. Instead, they graze until they get a מום (blemish).

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This phrase opens an answer to a contradiction.

steps.confusionAlert: 'They graze' does not mean the animals lose their holiness. They stay holy. We simply do not offer them, because offering them would create a risk of disqualification.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first piece of the answer. The גמרא resolves the contradiction by assigning each of the three ברייתות to a different opinion. The 'graze' ruling is tied to the רבנן's rule against bringing קדשים into a situation that risks disqualification. The other two rulings are explained on the next amud.
